narration.text: The SDD Orchestrator is live! And it's here to make Spec-Driven Development easier for you to run. You already know the idea behind it is solid — start with clear intent, generate the right artifacts, review the work, and keep the evidence tied to the feature. But in practice, it's easy to lose your footing. Which skill should I run first? What artifacts do I need in place to begin? How do I know Codex and I are aligned? Where is this feature in the SDD lifecycle? And how do I know we did not drift out of scope? This is where the SDD Orchestrator comes in. It's not another skill for you to memorize. It's the guided path through the skills you already have. Start with a Jira ticket, ask Codex to run the Orchestrator, then move through the workflow with it, one step at a time. You move through it all in order — requirements intake, design, implementation planning, Jest unit tests, then Playwright validation. And the whole time, the Orchestrator keeps your run stateful — it remembers what you've finished, flags what still needs your review, and keeps your evidence connected as the feature moves through the lifecycle. If you're an engineer, that means less guesswork, easier parallel work, and a lot less lost context. Product managers get clearer traceability back to requirements. Engineering managers get a visible, repeatable path to adoption. And all of us get a shared way to keep improving Spec-Driven Development together. Try out the SDD Orchestrator on your next feature. Let’s team up to test, scale, and shape it together.
